Canada Post- Kevin Healy, Doug Strangward - Site Locations. 
The representatives from Canada Post were unable to attend due to weather 
conditions. The planner displayed the map of Canada Post's proposed site 
locations in Diamondvale and explained that the implementation date for the new 
mailboxes is planned for March, 1996. 
b) 
Community Health Council - Judy Guichon, Terry Frizzell, Dr. Brackley. 
Judy Guichon, Chairperson of the Community Health Council spoke first, giving 
a synopsis of the past year's work by the Health Council and the timetable for 
the transfer of control from the Health Ministry to the Regional Health Boards is 
Apr.1/96. There have been discussions of amalgamation of services within 
communities, across agency lines. 
Terry Frizzell, Administrator of the Nicola Valley Health Care Society spoke on 
the downsizing of acute care facilities and transfer of programs within the 
community. The hospital is hiring a social worker for the position of Discharge 
Planner to coordinate discharge with home support services. NVGH has been 
reduced to a twenty five (25) bed facility from forty five (45) beds. 
Dr. Graham Brackley, Chief of Staff at NVGH explained the rationale behind the 
elimination of first time deliveries at NVGH. The hospital has no anesthetist on 
staff, therefore no provision for emergency cesarean sections is available. In 
1995, the hospital sent 50% of their first time deliveries to Kamloops after 
complications developed during labour. The hospital staff feels the health risks 
are too great to carry on providing this service to the public. 
At 8:05 p.m., the three (3) representatives from the Community Health Council left the 
meeting, leaving three (3) members of the General Public remaining.

Outlined 
At Health Minister Joy MacPhail's request, the 
regionalization assessment team is developing a 
consultation process to solicit the input of those 
groups affected by health care reform. 
''When the assessment was announced, the 
Minister made it clear the review would not be 
another royal commission," said team chair Mike 
Farnworth. "However, we will obviously want to 
talk quite extensively to the RHB and CHG 
members who have been working with 
regionalization since the beginning." He added 
the team is making every effort to meet with as 
many groups affected by regionalization as 
possible, to ensure its' recommendations 
represent the broad range of perspectives held 
by the various groups in the health care field. 
These groups will include health employers, 
health care unions, the aboriginal community 
and physicians. Farnworth said the committee 
would also accept written submissions based on 
a questionnaire now being developed. 
The team has asked Jack Gerow, a former 
member of the North Shore Health Board, to 
assist with the consultation in order to expand its 
ability to meet with as many groups as possible. 
While stressing the agenda was still under 
development, Farnworth said the team is 
determining the best way to consult with boards 
and councils, which may include travelling to a 
number of B.C. communities, depending on the 
length of the summer legislative session. "Given 
the legislative demands that require caucus 
members to be in the House, most meetings will 
be conducted in Victoria," said Farnworth. 
1996 Elections Suspended 
During Assessment 
Planned fall elections to Regional Health Boards 
and Community Health Councils have been 
suspended following a request from the caucus 
assessment team. 
Health Minister Joy MacPhail sent a letter to all 
board and council chairs this week indicating the 
elections proposed for November 1996 would be 
suspended. Her decision reflected an interim 
recommendation presented by the assessment 
team, who requested the elections be 
suspended in order not to influence or conflict 
with the final recommendation they will make on 
the process at the end of the summer. 
The elections were to select partial membership 
to all CHCs, and to the RHBs in Victoria, 
Vancouver, Burnaby, North Shore and 
Richmond. "Our job as members of the 
assessment team is to explore all aspects of the 
regionalization process, including the process of 
selecting board and council members," said 
team chair Mike Farnworth. "Considering the 
time frame involved, it would simply be 
impractical for the government to proceed with 
the elections this fall." 
MacPhail stressed that her response to the 
interim recommendation should not be 
interpreted as a final opinion on board and 
council elections. Rather, it is simply a practical 
decision that recognizes that there are widely 
divergent views on the best way to ensure 
effective public participation in our health care 
system. 
"It will be our job to consider all of these views 
and recommend a course of action, "said 
Farnworth.

SUMMARY OF PRELIMINARY FINDINGS: AUGUST 9, 1996 
The UBCM New Directions in Health Task Force has undertaken a survey of its members' 
experiences and views with respect to the New Directions in Health plan. Its purpose is to contribute 
to the work of the Regionalization Assessment Team. These preliminary findings are based on 70 
UBCM members who have responded to date. 
The concept of New Directions is supported by almost all respondents. As well, the majority are 
universally critical of the implementation experience. The Ministry ofHealth is criticized for lack 
of clear, consistent leadership and respondents advise the Ministry to be decisive, but not to be 
unilateral (many see it as both indecisive and unilateral). The Ministry is expected to provide the 
framework, the ground rules and the guidelines for implementation while recognizing that these must 
allow for variability to ensure relevance and responsiveness to local conditions. 
With respect to the key components of new Directions, as presently planned, there is greater support 
for the community health councils (CHCs) then for regional health boards (RHBs). In non-urban 
areas the latter are seen by some as another layer of bureaucracy and the argument is made that there 
should be only one body operating within redefined boundaries. In two metropolitan areas the 
regional board is viewed as the important body and CHCs should either be purely advisory or not 
developed at all. 
Direct elections to RHBs/CHCs are favoured by the largest number of respondents. There is strong 
support for the coordination and rationalization of community health services. There is significant 
support for the decentralization of health budget management from Victoria, but there is a difference 
of opinion as to whether this should be managed regionally or at a community level. 
Rural respondents have distinct priorities. Ensuring basic emergency and medical services is 
important The issue of funding and access to services is part of this as well (whether population or 
distance from services should drive funding). 
Regarding the implementation of New Directions, respondents are virtually unanimous that the 
Government needs to decide now about the future of New Directions. The majority advise that it 
proceed, but with the changes suggested and on a phased-in approach according to regional and 
community readiness. It is evident that too much change has already occurred to go back to the health 
world before New Directions.
